images.alt: Humans give off heat, which warms the air surrounding them. In calm conditions this layer of warm air stays close to the skin, so the person feels warmer. Strong winds quickly remove this layer of warm air replacing it with cooler air, which makes us feel colder. The quicker the wind the faster the layer is removed and the colder we feel. Wind Chill Explained

post.text:
🍃 Strong winds and frigid air mean bitterly cold southerlies are on the cards 🧊

🥶 Strong Wind Watches for the lower South Island coinciding with cold air will result in very low wind chill values, possibly as low as -2°C for Invercargill on Friday afternoon.

source.agency_name: Meteorological Service of New Zealand (MetService NZ)
